text:
If you've still got evening plans, the sky's mostly cooperating: any leftover showers should wind down by 8, leaving a partly cloudy, mild night settling into the upper 50s. Winds are light out of the west, so nothing to worry about if you're out on the water early on, though the lake goes quiet and clear for the rest of the night.

Wednesday is the reward day. Sunshine takes over, highs climb to around 81, and the air's clean with good quality all around. Models are tight on this one, so I'm confident in a genuinely nice midweek day. The lake stays calm too, waves a foot or less, easy conditions if you want to get out on the water after work. Enjoy it while it lasts, because Thursday brings another round of showers and some possibly strong thunderstorms back into the picture.

week.blurb: Scattered showers linger into afternoon under a high near 75; the Euro's far wetter, so keep the umbrella handy.
Mostly sunny and warmer, high near 81, models all agree it stays dry.
Afternoon showers and thunderstorms build, high near 84, with gusty south wind and a real severe risk.
A cooler front brings scattered showers and storms, high near 80, best chances midday into afternoon.
Sunny, crisp, and dry all day, high near 78, about as good as August gets.
Mostly sunny and mild, high near 82, with rain holding off until after dark.
Humidity returns with showers and thunderstorms likely, high near 81, especially by afternoon.

WCAX METEOROLOGIST: A secondary cold front crosses the region Friday, bringing additional scattered showers and thunderstorms (40% chance), mainly across central and southern Vermont during the afternoon, with highs cooling to near 76°. High pressure anchors over Vermont and the North Country for the weekend, delivering a picture-perfect stretch of weather with bright sunshine, highs in the upper 70s to low 80s, and crisp overnight lows in the 50s. Returning humidity and an approaching cold front bring scattered shower and storm chances late Monday (50% chance) into Tuesday.
